evidence.note: Wikipedia's article on the film says its US copyright was not renewed in the 28th year, so it entered the public domain in 1965. That claim is not a primary record. I could not read the S section of the 1964 and 1965 Catalog of Copyright Entries motion-picture volumes, because the fetched text was truncated. Absence of a renewal is therefore not confirmed.

editorial:
Swing High, Swing Low is a Paramount picture released March 12, 1937. Mitchell Leisen directed Carole Lombard and Fred MacMurray. Charles Butterworth, Jean Dixon, Dorothy Lamour and Harvey Stephens are also in the cast. The story follows Maggie King and the soldier Skid Johnson, who meet in Panama and become involved in a nightclub brawl. Its source is the 1927 Broadway play 'Burlesque' by George Manker Watters and Arthur Hopkins. A creator would want it for the Lombard–MacMurray pairing and for the Panama and nightclub settings. Copies are already widely circulated on the Internet Archive.

The trap is that the film's non-renewal rests only on a secondary claim. Wikipedia says the claimants did not renew in 1964–65, but I did not confirm that in the Catalog of Copyright Entries volumes. A separate trap is the underlying play. If 'Burlesque' was renewed, that could still reach the story, and nobody has checked it. Do the primary renewal check for both the film and the play before relying on this title. Also treat the Internet Archive colorized 4K upload as separate added work.
faq: Is Swing High, Swing Low free to reuse in the US?

Not confirmed yet. Wikipedia says the 1937 copyright was not renewed in 1964–65, but I could not verify that against the Catalog of Copyright Entries. The underlying 1927 play 'Burlesque' also needs a renewal check. Verify both before commercial reuse.
Can I use the colorized 4K version on the Internet Archive?

Don't assume you can. Colorization is added material that can carry its own claim. If the black-and-white print's status is confirmed, use a plain black-and-white copy instead, not the colorized upload.
